## **Pricing and paywall** {#theme-pricing_paywall}

<!--ir-theme:pricing_paywall-->
   **Pricing and paywall.**
      14 recent review(s) mention pricing and paywall.
      Review window: Feb 22, 2026 - Jul 18, 2026
      **Why it matters:** Users mention price, subscriptions, or paywalls. This can signal pricing sensitivity in the niche.

         **Review examples:**
            1. _CookiesPrincess21_, Jul 18, 2026, 1/5: "I’ve had to block various accounts from trying to charge my card. Each with a different amount each time, even after blocking and changing my card number they continue to attempt to charge my card. I canceled my subscription months ago and they’re still attempting to charge."
            2. _Brooke the child_, Jul 15, 2026, 1/5: "This app keeps trying to charge me after I have cancelled. TG I put in my Apple Cash as payment when I did a trial or I’d have to fight every month to get 50 bucks back."
            3. _ZTM - 96_, Jul 14, 2026, 1/5: "Have barely even used the app, I forgot to set up the notifications to have it delivered to me in my phone’s Focus settings, but this is not about that, this is about what they do when you give them your card details for a free trial. I got the one week and realized I just never saw the notifications for it, so I went to cancel it, and it gave me the option to extend it for one week, so I thought maybe, why not, and extended it and marked down the exact date it would renew, so I could go online and cancel it. Little did I know, they hid a whole other charge underneath the main one for the only app of theirs I had an account on, a “bundle” subscription on top of the one I was signing up for a trial for, for apps I did not even have. I never attempted to cancel that one because I didn’t even know I had given them consent to attempt to charge me for it at all. This morning, I received a message from my bank stating that they blocked a fraudulent charge, and a website’s name. Since I was not expecting any charges, because the date for the renewal was not for a week, I stated that it was not me who attempted the charge, and immediately my card got cancelled and now I have to wait around for a new one, and I have to go through and update my card information now for all my bills. All because of this incredibly deceptive and scammy app that I never even got around to using. I am irritated beyond measure and dearly hope they get hit with a class action lawsuit, any business this scummy with trying to get your money is not worth a cent on principle. If they had a product good enough, they would just be upfront about everything and allow the product to speak for itself, ESPECIALLY since it appears that they target ND people and those with ADHD, meaning they target those who are most likely to forget to track their subscriptions and how many times they got charged for something. Honestly, just disgusting overall and I am so irritated by the utter inconvenience, I would give it zero stars everywhere if I could. Never ever give them your card info, only get your free trials through the App Store and remember to cancel as soon as you decide it is not for you!"
<!--/ir-theme-->

## **Bugs and stability** {#theme-bugs_stability}

<!--ir-theme:bugs_stability-->
   **Bugs and stability.**
      1 recent review(s) mention bugs and stability.
      Review window: Jun 25, 2026 - Jul 16, 2026
      **Why it matters:** Users mention crashes or instability. Treat as actionable only when volume spikes or follows an update; otherwise it is often baseline noise.

         **Review examples:**
            1. _Trigger_786_, Jul 16, 2026, 1/5: "Great at first, but the more you get into it, the more bugs and strange content you find. The support team can’t access any screenshots you attach to their help request form, and they repeatedly email you asking for a description of the issue that you already described."
            2. _Grievousnix_, Jun 25, 2026, 1/5: "One star, and only because zero isn't an option. The app itself is fine — but the subscription is a roach motel: easy to get in, engineered to be impossible to leave. Cancellation is buried behind dark patterns: guilt-trip screens, "are you sure you want to abandon your goals" prompts, hidden menus, and flows that loop you back instead of actually cancelling. A company confident in its product lets you leave in two taps. Fabulous instead bets you'll give up trying. I won't recommend an app that treats wanting to cancel as a bug to be patched out. Avoid until they make cancellation as frictionless as signup."
            3. _mink3eyki_, Jun 27, 2026, 2/5: "The App looks detailed and interesting but I’m very confused by the pricing. I click on one button for the membership it says ca. 70€, I click on another its 42€ something. I get a notification for a special deal, half price, since I gave feedback on the app but its somehow 52€, the next day I click on it it’s 48€? I actually want to buy the app but I feel I might get ripped off 😅 Edit: I got the app now for 39€.. but the “journey” is broken it only shows a white screen pls fix that Years later: wanted to Start again but the Same Price confusion (one Button Says 48€ another 39€). Also a new bug: when I Click on the „motivators“ there is no Text.. so again I like the App I want to buy it but scared that it wont work properly.. Annoying that years later its still so buggy"
<!--/ir-theme-->
